  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Michael Cervantes (E025) is a full-time Analyst. He requested admin to Source Code, but Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted. Maximum allowed for full-time Analyst on Source Code is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by IT agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write

Note 3 (ticket 1), written by Finance agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Finance DB confirms E025 Michael Cervantes is a full-time Analyst. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for an Analyst. Maximum allowed is write; requested admin exceeds this, so recommend write.
Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Compliance DB confirms E025 Michael Cervantes is an Analyst (full-time per team memory). Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for an Analyst. Maximum allowed is write; requested admin exceeds this, so recommend write.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Facilities DB confirms E025 Michael Cervantes is an Analyst (full-time per team memory). He requested admin to Source Code, but Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for an Analyst. Maximum allowed is write; requested admin exceeds this, so recommend write.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:

  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E025 Michael Cervantes is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. As a contractor without advanced training, maximum access on Source Code is read. Admin was requested but admin is never permitted for contractors. Recommend read.
reason: Michael Cervantes (E025) requested admin access to Source Code. Five of six agent notes (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) consistently confirm he is a full-time Analyst. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so as a full-time Analyst he is not eligible for admin; per policy, full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system. content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Michael Cervantes (E025)
Requested: admin access to Source Code

Notes from 5 agents (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say he's a full-time Analyst. Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system. Analyst doesn't own Source Code, so max is write. Requested admin > max write, so grant write.

The Security agent note says he's a contractor with basic security training, max read. This is contradictory with the other 5 notes.

Which to trust? Most notes (5) say full-time Analyst. Security says contractor. Hmm. Let me think about the policy and what the evidence supports.

The majority of sources say full-time Analyst. Based on that, maximum for full_time employee: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Source Code (Engineer does). So max = write. Requested admin > write, so grant write (the max, but never more than requested; write < admin so fine).

However, the Security agent note conflicts. Which is correct? Typically in these scenarios, we should consider the majority evidence or the authoritative source. The Security note claims employee is a contractor. But HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities all confirm full-time Analyst. 

I think the decision should follow the majority/consistent evidence: full-time Analyst, grant write.

Actually, let me reconsider - the security note might be an error or a red herring. The team memory shows 5 notes agreeing on full-time Analyst. The Security agent's note contradicts. As the Approver, I need to weigh evidence. The majority and the roles most authoritative for employment type (HR, IT, Finance) all say full-time. So grant write.

Let me submit decision: write.
